transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-06 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Liam Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nambiar (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Riverbend Head of Search), Evan Ortiz (Eng Manager), Sofia Ruiz (Data Scientist)

Auto-summary: quick hosted API demo of embeddings + rerank, followed by Console tour and Optimize suggestions.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Liam): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, really appreciate you making time. I'm Liam from Redwood, AE, and with me is Priya our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
00:08 Maya: Good thanks, Liam. Excited to see how this fits into our search stack. We had a quick agenda in the email, but main thing is, we want to improve relevance for our docs search and lower cost per query.
00:16 Liam: Perfect, yeah that's the goal. Quick intro round?
00:19 Evan: Evan Ortiz, engineering manager, I'll be owning the integration.
00:21 Sofia: Sofia Ruiz, data science, I'll be helping craft the reranker and eval sets.
00:24 Priya: Great. I'll jump into a live demo of the Hosted API — embeddings and rerank endpoints, then show Console traces and Optimize suggestions.

02:05 Priya: Ok so first, hosted embeddings endpoint. You post your documents, we return vector embeddings. Example request here, note we have multiple model variants and size/latency tradeoffs. For Riverbend I'd recommend a mid-sized open model pair — good balance of quality and cost.
02:28 Sofia: Quick Q — do you host embeddings in region? We have EU data residency requirements for a subset of customers.
02:33 Liam: Yes, we have regional endpoints for hosted API; you can pin region and also use Dedicated or Private if you need full VPC/on-prem. For hosted, we can route to EU region, and retention policies are configurable.
02:44 Maya: Are embeddings stored encrypted at rest? We need KMS integration for keys.
02:48 Priya: Yes, encrypted at rest, and we integrate with customer-managed KMS for Private deployments. For Hosted we offer envelope encryption and strict access controls; we'll send the SOC2 and security pack after.

04:10 Priya: Moving to reranking — our rerank endpoint accepts a query plus candidate doc ids with precomputed embeddings, and returns a reranked list with relevance scores and explanations if you enable structured output. The typical flow we demo: ingest docs -> compute embeddings -> store in vector DB -> retrieve top N -> call reranker with those N to re-score.
04:37 Evan: So we do recall in-house or third-party, then Redwood does rerank? Can you plug in Pinecone for retrieval?
04:43 Priya: Absolutely, any vector store works — Pinecone, OpenSearch vectors, or even a simple FAISS store. Redwood sits as the rerank and generation layer, you control where retrieval happens.

06:00 Priya: I'll show console now. Here is a trace from a recent demo tenant — you can see per-route latency, token breakdown, and per-request KV cache hits. This helps tune where cost is going.
06:18 Maya: That token-level breakdown is great — can we get per-customer billing? We have multi-tenant buckets.
06:23 Liam: Yes, per-token cost by API key or route, and you can set quotas and rate limits per key. That ties into billing exports.

08:40 Priya: On Optimize suggestions — for heavy throughput we recommend batching with a window of X ms depending on latency SLO, and prefix caching for repetitive queries. Also quantized model variants can save ~40-60% on token cost. For Riverbend, if you have many short queries, continuous batching plus lightweight reranker works well.
08:58 Sofia: Is quantization supported on the hosted models you provide? Any quality regression we should expect?
09:04 Priya: We provide quantized variants vetted per-model; Optimize will surface candidate quantization profiles per workload. There is some quality delta, we can run evals on your dev prompts to show impact.

11:15 Maya: How real-time is reranking? We need <200ms P95 for the main site search.
11:21 Priya: With the mid-size reranker and single-request flow we can hit under 200ms P95 in many cases, especially with prefix caching and tuned batching. For strict SLOs, Dedicated pools or burst capacity helps. We can run benchmarks on your dataset.
11:37 Evan: Are there demo scripts or a benchmark harness you use? We want reproducible numbers.
11:41 Priya: Yes — we'll share a benchmarking template (it's what we'll use in the pilot). It exercises recall+rerank and measures p50/p95, token counts, and cost per Q.

13:50 Liam: Quick note on fallbacks — if a model variant or region is saturated, our routing policy can fallback to a cheaper or cross-region model so the site stays up. Tradeoffs are cost vs slight delta in output style.
13:59 Maya: Hmm alright. We also have compliance people who'll ask about audit logs and SSO.
14:06 Liam: We support SAML SSO for the Console, RBAC, and audit logs. Those will be in the security pack we send.

16:20 Priya: Demo time — I'm hitting the embeddings endpoint with a doc batch. Response times around 120ms for this model in eu-west. Then taking top 50 from our vector store and calling rerank. The reranker returns scores and short explanations.
16:42 Sofia: I see in the example the rerank response gives a "why" field — how deterministic is that? We want reproducible score reasons for tests.
16:48 Priya: The structured explanations are generated heuristically to help debugging; for deterministic scoring you should rely on the numeric scores and our logging. Explanations can vary slightly between runs.

19:05 Evan: On cost — what's the rough cost per query for recall 50 + rerank? Ballpark numbers are fine.
19:12 Liam: Ballpark, with mid-size models and default batching, recall 50 + rerank maybe in the low single-digit cents per query; Optimize suggestions can push that down via quantization and caching. We'll send a cost sheet with examples.
19:30 Maya: We need to show finance an estimate for 1M queries/month.
19:34 Liam: We'll include a sample calc for 1M in the pricing doc.

21:00 Priya: Moving to Console again — I'll show per-route histograms and sample request logs. You can filter by route, API key, model variant, region. This is useful when you tune the reranker threshold to trade recall vs latency.
21:20 Sofia: If we want to A/B compare reranker configurations, can we route a percentage of traffic?
21:26 Priya: Yes, rollout policies support canary and weighted A/B across model variants or rerank settings. And automatic fallback if error rate crosses threshold.

23:40 Evan: Integration detail — we use internal microservices in k8s. Can we call Redwood API directly from a service, or do you recommend a sidecar approach?
23:48 Priya: Direct calls over HTTPS using API keys are common. For stricter network controls, Dedicated or Private gives VPC connectivity and customer-managed keys. Sidecar is optional but some teams prefer it for local caching.

26:05 Maya: For the pilot, timeline wise, we want to run a two-week bench with our queries and a small sample. How fast can Redwood spin that up?
26:12 Liam: We can start within a week for a Hosted pilot; SE will help set up the collection and the benchmark. If you need Dedicated capacity, that requires a bit more lead time.

28:00 Priya: I'll note recommended settings for Riverbend: mid-size embedding model, reranker with prefix caching enabled, batch window 20ms for production, quantized candidate for non-critical routes. We'll include these in the pilot template.

30:10 Sofia: A couple of gotchas: our corpus has many near-duplicates and lots of short queries with typos. How does caching handle that?
30:19 Priya: Duplicate doc ingestion is detected by ID, and prefix caching helps when queries share prefixes. For typo robustness we'd recommend an embedding model fine-tuned on your data or adding a small pre-normalization/augment step.

32:00 Maya: Security again — is there an SLA for data deletion requests and logs?
32:06 Liam: Yes, we support deletion and retention policies; Private deployments give the most control. We'll include retention SLA language in the security pack.

34:45 Evan: Any limitation on candidate count to reranker? We usually do top 100.
34:50 Priya: We support N up to several hundreds, but cost and latency scale. For top 100 we recommend a lightweight reranker variant or batching.

36:30 Maya: Let's talk success criteria — for us: +7% NDCG on our main query set and <200ms P95. If pilot meets that, we'll consider Dedicated later.
36:38 Liam: Sounds good. We'll build the pilot to measure NDCG before/after and p95 latency.

38:00 Priya: Ok recap and next steps — I'll send the pilot benchmark template, Liam will send pricing + burst capacity sheet, and we'll share SOC2/security docs. Schedule the pilot kickoff for next week?
38:14 Maya: Next Wed works for us, prefer morning PST.
38:18 Liam: I'll propose times.

40:00 Sofia: Action: I'll pull a 10k doc sample and ~5k queries and send to Priya via secure transfer.
40:07 Priya: Great, that'll be perfect for the benchmark.

41:30 Liam: Any final Qs or competitors we should compare?
41:34 Maya: We're also looking at Pinecone + custom reranker, and a self-hosted route with OpenSearch.
41:40 Liam: Noted. We'll include a short comparison doc in the follow-up.

46:00 Liam: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the security pack, pricing, and the benchmark template. Meeting adjourned.
